sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Zumaya language' (citing Blench 2006, Shryock 1997, Ethnologue, ALCAM 2012)
sources.note: Nothing; states the language is known only from about 10 words recorded by Barreteau from probably the last speaker at Ouro-Lamorde (Maroua); shift to Fulfulde.

sources.citation: Shryock, Aaron. 1997. The classification of the Masa group of languages. Studies in African Linguistics 26(1): 29-62.
sources.note: Nothing. p.33: 'Zumaya has only a few remaining speakers [Barreteau 1987]. Its classification in the group is unclear because the language has not been well documented.' No Zumaya forms are used in the reconstruction; the only prosodic remark (p.~47) concerns lexical tone on nouns in the other Masa languages.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel (ed.). 1987. Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad: journees d'etudes les 4 et 5 septembre 1984. Paris: ORSTOM. 217 pp. [whole volume, Horizon IRD fdi:25258]
sources.note: Nothing on Zumaya beyond the essay above; p.13 abstract names baldamu and zumaya as 'deux langues en voie d'extinction'. Searched the full text layer for zumaya: no other data.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel. 1987. Un essai de classification lexico-statistique des langues de la famille tchadique parlees au Cameroun. In D. Barreteau (ed.), Langues et cultures dans le bassin du lac Tchad, 43-77. Paris: ORSTOM (Colloques et Seminaires). [Horizon IRD fdi:25260]
sources.note: Nothing. p.51: 'nous ne disposons que d'une dizaine de mots sur le zumaya (groupe masa), langue quasiment disparue'; pp.61-62 print two Zumaya items (bouche vun(anu), oeil aray); p.72 lists '46. zumaya' as the northern subgroup of groupe masa. This ~10-word ALCAM list is the language's entire documentation.
